key_insight: CLExEval shows that LLMs can sound clinically convincing while still making wrong diagnoses, so reasoning quality must be evaluated beyond final answers.
clinical_relevance: For medical AI, expert-checked evaluation is essential because fluent explanations and automated judging can substantially overestimate real clinical reliability.
method: Human-in-the-loop evaluation framework with progressive information masking
5,600 expert-physician annotations across 200 reasoning traces from 40 rare diagnostic cases
Comparison of model diagnoses, reasoning traces, and LLM-as-a-Judge behavior
evidence_signal: On 40 rare cases, GPT-4o-mini accuracy fell from 95.0% to 32.5% under scarcity, and a human-verified failure set of 142 cases showed GPT-4o-mini approved 47.9% of clinically incorrect outputs.
watch_item: The findings highlight that automated evaluators may miss clinically important errors, so deployment decisions should not rely on LLM judges alone.
paper_title: CLExEval: A Human-in-the-Loop Framework for Qualitative Evaluation of LLM Clinical Reasoning
